subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static armoured hauler truck model with a cab, turret, sealed cargo pod, and surface details like hazard stripes, neon strips, and glow headlights, skipping joints since it's non-rigged.

Now I'm working out precise dimensions and placement for the chassis, six wheels on front and rear axles, and the cab geometry, including a sloped hood built from an extruded profile along the vehicle's length.

Placing the windshield plane at its midpoint with a glowing scanline visor texture, then adding headlight boxes, a dark bumper wedge, and grille detailing on the nose before starting the cargo pod geometry.

Defining pod geometry...

Still shaping the pod geometry...

Now I'm thinking through end caps and the rear door: a smaller octagon extrusion caps both ends, with a hazard-textured plane for the rear door and a gap left for a coupling box near the cab. For armor, I'm planning side skirt plates along the chassis, fitted carefully between the wheel arches.

Now I'm placing a roof turret on the cab with a cylindrical base, twin forward-aimed barrels with muzzle glow, positioned above the cab roof. I'm also adding a light bar, antenna, and exhaust stack cylinders flanking the pod's sides.

Adjusting the exhaust stack positions to avoid overlapping the pod and cab gap, then adding neon underglow strips along the chassis bottom in cyan and magenta, red glowing rear lights, and detailing the wheels with dark tires, glowing cyan hub rims, steel hub caps, and dual rear axles.

I'm checking floor clearance so the wheels sit flush at y=0, then sizing the chassis box and verifying wheel widths poke slightly outside the chassis for a proper stance, while the wider cab needs clearance over the wheel arches.

I notice the wheels clip slightly into the cab bottom, so I'm raising the cab's extrusion to y=1.35, then positioning the octagonal pod above it from y=1.3 to 3.9 so it clears the rear wheels. Now I'm defining the octagon's chamfered corner coordinates for the pod shape.

Now I'm planning the textures needed: a glowing cyan HUD windshield, a shield emblem with "CONVOY" and pod ID text, yellow/black hazard stripes for the rear door, a grille texture, and a rear door seal detail.

I'm also sketching the turret sensor lens, cab door decal, pod seal strip with glow boxes, ribbed pod top panels with an antenna dish, and hex cargo-lock plates at the corners, settling on a palette of dark navy hull, slate armor, and orange, cyan, magenta, yellow accents. Defining the hull paint...

I'm working through texel density math to make sure panel seams stay visible at the chosen texture resolution, deciding the standard paint resolution won't resolve fine seams cleanly so I'll write a custom panel paint function with explicit seam width control based on UV fraction near panel boundaries.

Now I'm sketching the box-building helper and confirming parts can exist without joints for static geometry, then planning glow materials for flat-colored parts and plane decals for textured surfaces like a glowing windshield, before moving on to laying out the wheel positions along the body.

Defining the cab profile now, sweeping it along the x-axis to build the convex hull shape, then checking the windshield slope angle to figure out the correct normal for that panel.

I'm placing side window panes on the left and right faces with a dim cyan glow texture, then moving on to add a door number plate, hood details, and a hazard plate on the front bumper.

Placing headlight boxes near the nose, positioning a grille plane on the front face, and adjusting for the slight slope of the nose geometry...

Continuing on the turret design, I'm adding the body box with a glowing sensor-lens front, dual barrel rods extending forward with muzzle glow rings, and checking clearances against the cab roof and nose. Now I'm thinking about whether to add side skirt plates or armor along the cab for extra detail.

Placing a magenta glow strip along the cab sides and a thinner neon strip along the chassis, then adjusting positioning so the chassis neon doesn't collide with the wheels by confining it to the skirt panel region. Adding skirt panels with a hazard-stripe texture on the outer face and a glow strip underneath for extra detail.

Now I'm working on the rear end: placing a bumper box, red glowing tail lights, and dark mud flaps behind the rear wheels, checking that their positions don't overlap with the wheel geometry. I'm also setting up the main pod extrusion along the z-axis and starting on its end caps.

Door texture fits within the octagon cap bounds; I'll design it as a hazard-striped octagon with dark center, glowing cyan lock ring, and "SEALED" text, adding a separate glow disc plane near the lock to avoid washing out the whole texture.

Now I'm positioning the pod bands around the hull: extruded octagon rings with chamfered corners, thin orange-trimmed dark bands placed at a few z-positions along the body, checking they clear the wheel wells without clipping the main hull or rear wheels.

I'm also placing the side emblem and ID plate decals at specific x/z offsets between the bands, verifying each plane's width and center position stays clear of the band footprints so nothing overlaps.

Then I'm nudging the emblem plate slightly off the hull surface to avoid z-fighting, and sketching a glow strip for the top flat face along with the top ribs, sizing each to fit within the octagon's flat width.

Now I'm thinking about adding a sensor mast with a glowing tip to the pod top, considering and then skipping extra hex lock plates for simplicity, and planning cyan glow strips along the midpoints of the diagonal chamfer panels.

Working out box rotations for each chamfer strip...

Now I'm placing smaller cab details: a door emblem decal mirrored on both sides positioned under the window, skipping a bull bar for the front grille, and figuring out where exhaust stacks should sit relative to the pod's front cap chamfer.

Checking a few collision spots for the stacks against the cab roof and pod cap, I decide to mount them on the cab roof edge instead, with glowing orange tips, keeping them clear of the turret base positioned further back.

Now I'm moving to the texture SVGs: a hazard stripe pattern on a dark background, an emblem badge with a hex shield and "HX-7 CONVOY" text, and an octagon door texture with dashed yellow hazard stroke and a "SEALED" label.

Writing visor, grille, and eye textures...

Now I'm thinking through a plating paint function that resolves colors and mixes them based on the panel's dominant axis.

Glow comes from kits/glow. Part count is light at ~120, so I want to push toward 180+ by adding tread lugs on the wheels (10 boxes per wheel, rotated around the axle angle) and rib details on the pod top to bulk out the detail without much complexity.

Checking lug placement so the bottom-most lugs don't clip through the floor — adjusting tire radius and lug height so clearance stays above the 2% threshold. For tire coloring I'll just use a flat dark paint rather than a mottled texture, then write out each lug as its own part.
